purpose: Teach: 買い手/忠告/転用/模範/必読/預かっ/コーディネート/休養

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 創業時、買い手を、必死に、探した日々、本当に、覚えているぞ、お父さんから、お前に、伝えていきたい、絶対、創業精神、忘れるな、本当に、絶対だ。
lines.en: When we were just starting out, I remember those days of desperately searching for buyers. I want to pass this on to you — never forget the founding spirit. That's absolute.
lines.style: Slow, measured opening. Weight on each sentence. Pauses between thoughts as if reaching back through time. Quiet conviction, not force. The voice of someone who has earned the right to say 'absolute.'

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。お父さんからの忠告、私、本当に、いつも、心に、刻んでおります、社員にも、伝えていきます、絶対、創業精神、引き継いでまいります、本当に。
lines.en: Yes. Your advice, Father — I carry it in my heart always. I will pass it on to my staff, and I will inherit the founding spirit without fail. Truly.
lines.style: Formal but not stiff. Clear-eyed sincerity. Each phrase lands with quiet responsibility. Respectful distance maintained, but genuine warmth underneath. The tone of a son who has become a leader and still feels the weight of that watching.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 創業時の機械、新しい用途に、転用していくこと、お父さん、推奨していたぞ、お前にも、本気で、考えて欲しい、本当に、頼むぞ、絶対だ、これは。
lines.en: The equipment we used when we founded this — repurposing it for new uses, that's what I recommended to you back then. I want you to think seriously about this. Please. I'm asking you, absolutely.
lines.style: Slight lean forward. Concrete and specific, not abstract. A light tap of urgency on 'seriously.' The voice of someone who has seen how good ideas die without follow-through. Gentle but firm.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。お父さんが、社員、模範として、生きた姿、本当に、私の心に、ずっと、残っております、感謝しております、お父さん、本当に、絶対に、お父さん。
lines.en: Yes. The way you lived — as a model for your staff, Father — it has stayed with me always. My heart carries it still. I'm grateful. Truly grateful.
lines.style: Soft opening. Voice slightly thickened with emotion but held in check. Pause before 'grateful' — not performed, but felt. Trailing tenderness at the end, like speaking to someone no longer there.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 創業時、お父さん、必読書、いつも、お前にも、教えてやりたかった本、いっぱい、あるんだぞ、本当に、いつか、共有しような、ね、約束、絶対。
lines.en: When we started, there were so many books I always wanted to teach you — the ones I read, the essential ones. I have so many of them. Someday let's share them together. That's a promise. Absolute.
lines.style: Warming, more conversational now. A small wistfulness on 'wanted to teach.' The rhythm becomes almost gentle, almost playful in its warmth. Steadies on the final promise — certain, not forced.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。創業以来、お得意様から、お預かった、信頼、本当に、絶対、守ってまいります、お父さんの代から、続く、お約束、絶対です、本当に、お父さん。
lines.en: Yes. Since our founding, I have been entrusted with the trust of our valued customers. I will protect it absolutely. From your generation forward, that promise continues. I promise you, Father.
lines.style: Solemn and steady. The cadence of someone speaking an oath. Anchored, grounded. Not rushed. Each phrase is a brick laid down. The respect is evident but not performative — simply how a leader speaks when honoring what was given to him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: お父さんの代の、新製品のコーディネート、創業者として、関わってきた、本当に、楽しい思い出だった、お前の代でも、頑張れ、絶対、本当に、頼んだ。
lines.en: Back in your day, coordinating our new products — as a founder, I was so involved in that. Those were truly wonderful memories. Keep working hard in your time too. I'm asking you. Absolutely.
lines.style: A slight smile in the voice, nostalgia warming it. Not looking backward with regret, but with genuine affection. The tempo opens slightly — more room to breathe. Closes with gentle but certain insistence on the ask.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。お父さん、本当に、ゆっくり、休養を、お取りください、私、絶対、お父さんの代の、想いを、引き継いでまいります、本当に、信じてください、絶対。
lines.en: Yes. Father, please rest now. Take it slowly, take it easy. I will carry forward the spirit of your generation without fail. Please believe me. Absolutely.
lines.style: Tender but composed. The voice of someone giving permission to someone they love. Slightly breathier on 'rest' — genuine care, not obligation. Closes with quiet conviction and a touch of reassurance, as if saying: I have this now.
